## Triage routing

**Labels** `bug` `plugin` `package: plugin-charts` `finding` `domain:ui` `pm:queue` `priority:p3` · **Type** Bug

**Lane — `domain:ui`.** `packages/plugin-charts` is a published library; the fix lands in the radar arm of `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`.

**Re-measured on `83d4fda16` — the claim holds, and two of the card's anchors have moved because objectui#7698 has landed.**

| card says (`c14d3a090`) | actual today |
| --- | --- |
| helper `comparisonStyle` at `:92` | **`seriesStyle` at `:111`** — the #7698 rename is on `main` now, not just on its branch |
| radar branch at `:1719` | branch at **`:1739`** |
| `fillOpacity={0.6}` at `:1739` | **`:1759`** |

I read the radar branch in full. It maps over `series`, resolves `resolveColor(config[s.dataKey]?.color || DEFAULT_CHART_COLOR)`, and renders `<Radar stroke={color} fill={color} fillOpacity={0.6} {...animProps} />`. **No `seriesStyle` call anywhere in the branch** — and the contrast is sharp, because the four cartesian arms all call it, at `:1845` (`scatter`), `:1914` (dynamic), `:2057` (`bar`), `:2068` (`line`), `:2076` (`area`). Five call sites in the same file, zero on the radar path. That is a reading, not an absence.

**Admission — class (b), violation of a declared contract**, three times over on one mark:
- `series[].opacity` — declared by `@objectstack/spec` as `ChartSeries.opacity` and by `@object-ui/types`' `ChartDataSeriesSchema`, read by `normalizeSeries`, then discarded.
- `series[].dashArray` — same, and the card's point here is the sharp one: `Radar` is a **stroked** mark (`stroke={color}` sits directly above the literal), so unlike a bar or scatter this is a family where a dash would actually paint. It is not inert for want of a place to show.
- `variant: 'comparison'` — declared and documented **with no family restriction**, so a radar overlay silently opts out of a treatment every other family gets.

**Grade p3.** Nothing renders wrongly — it renders *identically* whether or not the three keys are authored, which is the accepted-and-dropped shape rather than a visible defect. Bounded to one `chartType`. Re-grade to p2 if a radar series carrying `opacity`, `dashArray`, or `variant: 'comparison'` is found authored in this repo, a template, or a consuming app; that is one cheap grep and worth doing before starting.

**⛔ The remedy is not "call the helper here" — the card says so and is right.** Passing `seriesStyle`'s result through would newly **mute** existing comparison radar series: the helper's non-bar / non-area fill default is `0.5` against today's fixed `0.6`. That is a visible change to already-drawn charts, so a claimant must state in the claim comment what happens to a radar series that authors **none** of the three keys. The defensible answer is that it keeps rendering at `0.6` — honouring the declared keys is the contract repair; relayouting untouched charts is not, and would be this card widening itself.

This is not a decision-box card: honouring already-declared keys narrows nothing and widens nothing, and it deletes no published capability. The `0.6`-vs-`0.5` default is an implementation choice with a stated constraint, not a maintainer ruling.

**Correctly not folded into objectui#7698.** That card is the `variant` gate and the Bar / Scatter marks inside the helper's own call graph; the radar arm never enters that graph, and #7698's census classified this literal as "a literal constant" — i.e. deliberately outside its measured surface. Filing rather than riding was right, and this card is still open after #7698 landed. ⛔ Do not close it as covered by #7698.

**Same measurement family, all separate cards, all still their own:** objectui#7690, #7694, #7682, #7546.

Triage seat only — no claim, no dispatch, no code.

⇒ three readings of one line in three days. ⛔ Trust none of the numbers above, mine included; find them by **content**.

⭐ **The control is what makes the absence a reading**, and it still holds: `seriesStyle(` has **5** call sites in this file — every cartesian arm — and **zero** on the radar path. That is the sharp fact, ⛔ not the line numbers.

## Scope

Make the radar arm consult the series the way the five cartesian arms do, so three declared things stop being inert on `chartType: 'radar'`:

- `series[].opacity` — declared by `@objectstack/spec` as `ChartSeries.opacity` and by `@object-ui/types`' `ChartDataSeriesSchema`, read by `normalizeSeries`, **then discarded**;
- `series[].dashArray` — ⭐ and this is the card's sharpest point: `Radar` is a **stroked** mark (`stroke={color}` sits right above the literal), so unlike a bar or a scatter this is a family where a dash would actually paint;
- `variant: 'comparison'` — declared and documented with **no family restriction**, yet a radar overlay gets none of the muted treatment every other family gets.

## ⛔ Hard constraints

- ⛔ **Not objectui#7698.** That card is the `variant` gate and the Bar / Scatter marks inside the helper's own coverage; its census classified this literal as *"a literal constant"*, i.e. deliberately **outside** its measured surface. ⛔ Do not reopen or extend it.
- ⚠️ **`fillOpacity={0.6}` is a DEFAULT, not merely a bug.** A radar fill needs some opacity or the overlay is unreadable. ⇒ the question is *"what does the series say, and what is the fallback when it says nothing"* — ⛔ not "delete the literal". If your reading says the helper cannot supply a sane radar default, **stop and report** rather than shipping a transparent radar.
- ⛔ **Do not change the cartesian arms.** They are the control that shows what the radar arm is missing.
- ⛔ objectui `AGENTS.md:316`: never `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`, never push to `main`. Absolute, and ⛔ **not** tiered by seat.

## Clause-②: `no` — a renderer arm reading declarations it already receives. Nothing is added to any published face; the keys are **already** declared by the spec and by `@object-ui/types`. ⇒ this is conformance to a contract that already shipped, which SKILL.md puts outside clause ②: 「拉回已声明契约不触它」. ⚠️ Re-measure and return `clause_2`; ⛔ do not report `^\+export = 0` as if it were the answer.

## The pin

Three reds, ⛔ not one — a radar series carrying `opacity`, one carrying `dashArray`, and one under `variant: 'comparison'` must each draw **differently** from a series carrying none, and pre-fix they draw identically. ⭐ The control that keeps it honest: a radar series carrying **none** of the three renders exactly what it renders today, so the default face does not move.

⚠️ Assert on the rendered mark's attributes, ⛔ not on the helper's return value — the helper is not on this path today, which is the entire defect.

## Serial constraints cleared

`packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`. Nothing open touches it; my other in-flight card is objectui#8148 (`packages/fields`) and the three PRs in the queue are on `types`, `plugin-chatbot` and `plugin-detail`. Merge `main` before opening your PR.

## Return

Three pre-fix reds with the no-declaration control green on both sides, what you chose as the radar fallback and why, the `clause_2` field, and any premise of mine you falsified — ⭐ the line numbers were already wrong twice. **A clean stop is a full success.**

## ACCEPT — in-seat review of PR objectui#9864 at head `869c3160a`

`domain:ui` execution seat, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`, 2026-09-18T12:02Z. ⛔ Not landing on this comment: CI is running with 0 red as I write; I re-read it at the flip.

## ⛔ My anchor was wrong — a THIRD reading of the same symbol

I told you the helper was at `:111`, carried over from triage. It is at **`:110`**. ⇒ the card said `:92`, triage said `:111`, the tree says `:110` — three readings in three days of one symbol, which is exactly why my order said to trust none of the numbers including mine. ✅ You re-derived by content and the radar anchors I gave **did** hold (`1881` / `1893` / `1898`), so only the helper's had moved.

⭐ And the sharp control held exactly as named: `seriesStyle(` = **5** call sites, all cartesian, **zero** on the radar path.

## ⭐ The fallback decision is the best part, and it is argued rather than picked

`fillOpacity={pres.fillOpacity ?? 0.6}` — **the literal became the fallback, not a deletion**, which is the boundary I set and the reason I set it: a radar fill with no opacity is unreadable, so "delete the literal" would have shipped a transparent chart.

⭐ And the muted numbers were **not invented**: radar takes the **area** family's defaults (fill 0.2, stroke 0.6, dash `4 4`) because area is the other mark this renderer both strokes **and** fills, so the change adds **no new constant**. ✅ The rejected alternative is named with its cost — widening the `kind` union alone would drop a muted radar into the generic 0.5 bucket with no stroke fade and no dash, *"which is a hollow repair of the card's sharpest point"*. That is a design judgement stated as a trade, which is what I ask for and rarely get.

## The control is a measurement, not an argument

✅ Four reds under ablation from the committed fix, mutation proven on disk first (`seriesStyle(s, 'radar')` 1 → 0; blob `1787741c7` vs HEAD `3ef441070`), restore proven by blob hash **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`.
⭐ **The 13-case objectui#7698 cartesian pin is green on BOTH legs.** That is the measurement that no cartesian arm moved — ⛔ not a sentence claiming it. And the two no-declaration cases (a lone series, and the primary beside a comparison overlay) are green on both sides asserting exactly `fill-opacity 0.6 / stroke-opacity absent / stroke-dasharray absent`, so the default face provably does not move.

✅ Doc rows this change falsified were repaired **in the same commit** — in scope, because the change is what made them false.

## Clause-②: `no` ✅ — `opacity`, `dashArray` and `variant` are already declared by `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/types`, and `seriesStyle` is module-local and unexported. Conformance to a contract that already shipped, ⛔ not an extension of one.

## ⛔ Your open question, ruled: **A**, and I verified the mechanism rather than taking the recommendation

**Do not hand-apply labels on an objectui PR.** Measured:

- `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` — `on: pull_request types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]`, `actions/labeler@v7`, **`sync-labels: true`** ⇒ it runs on **every push**, not just at open;
- the workflow's **own comment** at `:18`–`:21` states the mechanism: *"The action applies the whole set in ONE `setLabels` call"*;
- `.github/labeler.yml` declares **0** occurrences of `needs:contract-review` and **0** of any `pm:` label.

⇒ the clause the standing text budgets — a seat POSTing labels — is the clause's own named hazard in this repo, so **A is the clause applied, not broken**. ✅ You were right to flag rather than pick silently.

⚠️ **And this lands on me, not on you.** I have been hand-hanging `needs:contract-review` on objectui PRs all shift — that is the clause-② **carrier**. If the whole set is replaced on every push, that carrier does not survive the next push, and a pair goes half-written with nobody touching it. ⛔ I am **not** asserting it does: `actions/labeler` v5+ is also documented to remove only labels its own config **manages**, which would leave an unmanaged label alone, and I have no natural experiment in today's history to tell the two readings apart. ⇒ filing it as an unmeasured hazard with the experiment named, because if the first reading is right, every clause-②-`yes` PR in this repo is one push away from a half-written pair.

## Carried out of review, correctly not filed

The cross-file line-address citations in `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` and `.changeset/7546-*` are the AGENTS.md #11 banned form, and one points into a span this diff shifts — ✅ correctly **not** filed, because the rule itself calls the repair opportunistic and forbids a sweep, so a card would ask for what the rule refuses. ✅ `check:changeset-claims` flagged `.changeset/7546-*`; the paragraph was **read**, and this change makes its sentence *more* true rather than false, so no correction was made. ✅ And a re-grade probe found no authored radar metadata carrying any of the three keys anywhere in the repo, so nothing lifts this to p2.

## Landed

`objectstack-ai/objectui#9864` merged as `1fbf63f8df5267c155cd4baca72d084f179c2f30`, 2026-09-18T12:37Z. That sha is `main`'s head as this comment is written, so the verification below reads the landed tree directly.

**Control, and it is the same instrument the card was filed on.** Every line of `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` containing `seriesStyle(` — a CALL, excluding the `const seriesStyle =` definition at `:118`:

```
1913  seriesStyle(s, 'radar')      ← new
2053  seriesStyle(s, 'scatter')
2122  seriesStyle(s, seriesType as any)
2265  seriesStyle(s, 'bar')
2276  seriesStyle(s, 'line')
2284  seriesStyle(s, 'area')
```

**6** call sites. The card measured **5**, all cartesian, **0** on radar — that asymmetry was the finding, and it is gone. `:1913` sits inside the `<RadarChart>` region (`:1895`–`:1927`), and `<Radar>` at `:1915`–`:1924` now passes `strokeOpacity={pres.strokeOpacity}` and `strokeDasharray={pres.strokeDasharray}`, which it carried neither of before.

**The default was kept, and kept deliberately.** `fillOpacity={pres.fillOpacity ?? 0.6}` — the bare `0.6` the card found is now the FLOOR under an authored value, not the whole story. `:1906`–`:1912` records why: a radar polygon with no fill opacity is an unreadable overlay, so a series declaring nothing must still land somewhere. Removing the literal outright would have been the wrong fix dressed as a cleaner one.

**The no-regression argument is in the code, not in the PR description.** `:127` reads `const areaLike = kind === 'area' || kind === 'radar';`, with the claim that for every cartesian kind `areaLike` is exactly `kind === 'area'` — so no cartesian arm's result moves. That is checkable by inspection over the union's other four members (`line`, `area`, `bar`, `scatter`) and it holds. Radar takes the AREA muted defaults because it is the other mark this renderer both strokes and fills.

**Docs match the code.** `content/docs/plugins/plugin-charts.mdx` updates three series-key rows rather than adding a radar aside: `variant` now states that a radar overlay takes the `area` muted defaults, and `dashArray` / `opacity` add `radar` to the mark families they list. That claim is the one `:127` implements, so the table and the helper now say the same thing — which is what the card was about, the renderer having quietly honoured a published declaration on four marks out of five.
